findings.title: UsernameForm calls a method that does not exist
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate now calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method added on UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). There is no zero-arg overload anywhere in the hierarchy, so this class does not compile and the re-authentication skip change cannot build. The call is also in the branch where context.getUser() is already non-null, so it needs a passkeys-enabled check that does not depend on a missing overload.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys UI is skipped when the user is not yet known
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, and both authenticate() (line 115) and the error challenge() override (line 137) now gate WebAuthn form setup on that helper. Previously authenticate() filled passkey/conditional-UI data precisely when no user was selected, and the error challenge did the same when context.getUser() was null. On a normal first login the user is null, so the login page and invalid-password error page no longer get the WebAuthn challenge, rpId, or ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI. Conditional passkey login (discoverable and non-discoverable) therefore regresses; only the re-authentication path, where a user is already on the context, still initializes passkeys.
